---
title: CLI
description: teire scan runs Teire's own engine on a folder or any public GitHub repository and prints every change that reaches your code, with its lines. teire check turns that into a CI gate.
icon: SquareTerminal
---

```bash
npx teire-cli scan
```

The package is [`teire-cli`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/teire-cli) on npm. Installed globally, the command is `teire`:

```bash
npm install -g teire-cli
teire scan
```

To try it on a repository you haven't cloned, give its `owner/name` or URL. Teire downloads that commit as one archive into a temporary folder, scans it and deletes it:

```bash
npx teire-cli scan meridianlabs-ai/inspect_ai
```

This is a real run on [teire-dev/examples/ai-web](https://github.com/teire-dev/examples/tree/main/ai-web), with the path shortened:

```txt
Teire …/demo-ai-web
npm 5 direct + 75 transitive · 8 files · 7.0 s
APIs: OpenAI

Deadlines
  2026-04-30  Node.js 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30  passed · affected
  2026-10-23  gpt-4.1-nano shutdown  passed · affected

Affected (2)
  ● gpt-4.1-nano shutdown  priority 1 · 2 sites
    models/openai
    test/openai-stand-in.ts:14
    src/summarize.ts:13
  ● Node.js 20 reached end of life on 2026-04-30  1 site
    runtime/node
    package.json:8

1 more change checked, none reaching your code (--all lists them)

Notes
  4 model mention(s) not traced through wrappers or registries (Nemotron does this when TOKENFACTORY_API_KEY is set)
```

A group holds every change one pull request would fix, so a provider's retirements share a line: `o1-preview shutdown and 9 more`. The date beside it belongs to the change the title names. Product code is listed before tests and fixtures. In a terminal the current step shows on one line while the scan runs; a large repository takes a minute or two.

The scan makes the same engine calls as the Teire worker. Its findings match the dashboard once `TOKENFACTORY_API_KEY` is set, which lets Nemotron trace wrapped model IDs, for a repository with no organisation config. Packages are diffed and located on your machine. API and model changes come from Teire's [public catalog](/changes). For a provider the catalog hasn't read yet, the CLI reads that provider's pages itself, through the same quote gate.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `teire scan [target] [--json] [--all]` | Scan a folder (default: the current one), or a public GitHub repository as `owner/name` or its URL. `--all` also lists changes outside your installed versions |
| `teire check [target] [--fail-on affected\|deadline\|any] [--within 90]` | Exit 1 when the gate fails |
| `teire explain <change-id> [target] [--json]` | One change: summary, replacement, migration notes and the quoted sources. A package change ID is read from a scan of `target` |
| `teire changes [--provider p] [--ecosystem e] [--kind k] [--subject s] [--json]` | The public catalog. For a provider with a built-in reader whose changes the catalog doesn't hold yet, its pages are read on the spot |
| `teire mcp` | Serve the same tools to coding agents over stdio. See [MCP](/docs/build/mcp) |

## Gating CI

| `--fail-on` | Fails when |
|---|---|
| `affected` (default) | any change reaches your code |
| `deadline` | an affected change has a date within `--within` days (default 90), or already past |
| `any` | anything is affected, needs a person, or must be checked by hand |

Exit codes: **0** passed, **1** the gate failed, **2** a usage error or anything that went wrong. The same run with `teire check --fail-on deadline --within 60` ends:

```txt
teire check: 2 changes fail the "deadline" gate
```

```yaml title=".github/workflows/teire.yml"
name: teire
on: [pull_request, push]
jobs:
  deadlines:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - run: npx -y teire-cli check --fail-on deadline --within 60
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

## What it needs

Node.js 22 or newer. npm and Ruby need nothing else, because TypeScript and Prism are bundled. A missing toolchain becomes a note saying what to install, such as "go is not installed: install Go (https://go.dev/dl) or set TEIRE_GO". The other ecosystems are then still scanned.

| To read | Needs |
|---|---|
| Python packages | [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv), which supplies Python 3.12 and the pinned griffe and jedi. Without uv, a Python 3.11 or newer already installed gets a virtual environment with the same pins, made once in `~/.cache/teire` |
| Go modules | Go (`TEIRE_GO` for a specific binary) |
| Rust crates | `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --version 0.51.0 --locked` |
| Maven and Gradle | Java 17 or newer (`TEIRE_JAVA`); japicmp is downloaded once and checked against its SHA-1 |

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Higher GitHub rate limits for release notes, advisories and spec history |
| `TOKENFACTORY_API_KEY` | Nemotron traces model IDs through wrappers and registries, and reads discovered providers' pages |
| `TAVILY_API_KEY` | Searches for the notices of an API host neither the catalog nor the built-in readers cover |
| `TEIRE_URL` | Another Teire deployment (default `https://teire.vercel.app`) |

A package the repository doesn't pin is listed but not compared, and the notes count it: a Gemfile with no `Gemfile.lock`, or a Maven dependency whose version comes from a parent POM or BOM outside the repository. A diff that can't be computed (a release with no wheel, a download that timed out) becomes a "check by hand" item with its reason; the rest of the scan carries on.

`teire.yml` is honoured for `ignore`, `ecosystems`, `paths`, `ignorePaths`, `upgrades.cooldownDays` and `sources`.

<Callout title="What the CLI doesn't do">
  It reports and gates. It doesn't fix or open pull requests: fixes run in Teire's sandboxes, through the GitHub App or a [dry run](/docs/guide/public-scan#dry-run-a-fix).
</Callout>
